key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in perovskite films are not just defects—they are degradation hot spots that nucleate failure at impurity–perovskite interfaces.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a fast, non-invasive imaging-and-AI screening workflow to flag unstable perovskite films before device fabrication, supporting scalable quality control for solar cell manufacturing.
method: Nano-FTIR chemically identified harmful residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films.
High-resolution reflected-light microscopy plus machine-learning image analysis enabled rapid impurity detection in seconds.
Photo-stress and thermo-photo degradation tracking linked impurity density to early failure onset.
evidence_signal: Chemically validated imaging showed that degradation starts at impurity–perovskite interfaces, and films with higher impurity density exhibited accelerated early degradation.
watch_item: The workflow depends on calibration to chemically validated impurity signatures, so performance may vary across film compositions, processing routes, and imaging setups.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
